categoryNote: No disable-all-services option exists anywhere in NEXTRIX. Every service entry is single-purpose, detection-gated and journal-stamped; the schema never-touch list is enforced both by the validator and in code. Print Spooler is report-only by boundary.

tweaks.name: Startup app inventory & selective management
tweaks.description: Inventories every Run/RunOnce/Startup-folder item and enables or disables a selected item through the StartupApproved mirror.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner an accurate startup inventory and a per-item, journaled enable/disable control without ever editing or deleting the startup command.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxStartupInventory and Set-NxStartupItemState (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). The inventory covers HKCU/HKLM Run and RunOnce (64- and 32-bit), the per-user and common Startup folders, the Win32_StartupCommand view, and the StartupApproved mirror with its binary state decoded as Enabled (first byte 02) / Disabled (03) / Unknown. Selective management writes ONLY the StartupApproved binary marker - the same Task Manager enable/disable surface - and NEVER edits or deletes the Run value itself (WinUtil lesson: command values are not ours to rewrite). The exact prior bytes (or their absence) are captured and journaled before the write; verification re-reads the marker; rollback restores the exact bytes or removes the value when it never existed. RunOnce entries are inventory-only because Windows does not reliably honor a RunOnce approval mirror. Native application requires a journal root and -Approved (per-item explicit consent); -Plan performs captures and reports intent without writing. HKCU resolves to the invoking user when the engine runs elevated - stated as a limitation, never hidden.
tweaks.defaultState: Startup items enabled or disabled according to Windows defaults and prior user choices; no NEXTRIX approval marker exists.
tweaks.proposedState: Inventory available; individually selected startup items carry a journaled StartupApproved enable/disable marker.

verify.procedure: Inventory lists each item with approvalState; after Set-NxStartupItemState the marker is re-read and must show the intended Enabled/Disabled state. Journals a verify entry.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback delegates NX11 StartupApproved targets to Invoke-Nx11Rollback: exact original bytes are rewritten, or the value is removed when it never existed (only-if-ours).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue of the StartupApproved value (existed, kind, exact bytes) plus the Run/StartupFolder item identity, journaled before change.

sideEffects: A disabled startup app does not run at user sign-in; it can be re-enabled at any time.
Startup command values are never modified, so no application is uninstalled or reconfigured.
RunOnce entries are report-only (no reliable approval mirror).
HKCU targets the invoking user in an elevated engine session.
documentationSource: Research note: the StartupApproved binary encoding is community-established (E0 layer) and is journaled as exact bytes, never guessed.
Verification note 2026-11-23: the Task Manager startup-apps support article URL was checked and returned 404, so it is not cited; E1 rests on the documented Win32_StartupCommand class.

tweaks.name: Per-app background permissions (UWP)
tweaks.description: Moves one selected app between the documented AppPrivacy per-app background-permission lists.
tweaks.objective: Offer per-app background control while the global background-app permission remains owned by NX01-008.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxAppPermissionInventory and Set-NxAppPermission (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). Targets the machine policy multi-text lists under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\AppPrivacy: LetAppsRunInBackground_ForceAllowTheseApps, _ForceDenyTheseApps and _UserInControlOfTheseApps (value names verified in the local AppPrivacy.admx, build 26300). The global enum LetAppsRunInBackground belongs to NX01-008 and is never written here; this entry owns per-app lists only. Set-NxAppPermission reads all three lists, removes the selected PackageFamilyName from each, adds it to the chosen list (or removes every override), and writes each changed list through the NX11 journaled registry helper. Because the lists are REG_MULTI_SZ values, the read-modify-write preserves every sibling entry; the exact prior list is journaled per changed value. E0: the per-app list family is not covered by a verified Microsoft documentation URL - provenance is the local AppPrivacy.admx inspection plus the Policy CSP Privacy family already cited by NX01-008. Microsoft's CSP warning is surfaced: background denial can stop tile/notification updates and background mail sync.
tweaks.defaultState: No per-app AppPrivacy override lists set (or entries left by the user/other tools).
tweaks.proposedState: Selected app present in exactly one of ForceAllow / ForceDeny / UserInControl, with all sibling entries preserved.

verify.procedure: After Set-NxAppPermission, each changed list is re-read via Test-NxConfigurationState and must equal the intended REG_MULTI_SZ content; verify entries are journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled REG_MULTI_SZ list exactly (the core registry engine handles these targets); -Permission RemoveOverride removes only the selected app from every list.

originalState.method: The three per-app lists are captured in full before any write; only changed lists are journaled.

sideEffects: A denied app stops background updates, tile/notification refresh and background mail/voicemail sync (Microsoft CSP warning).
Open instances must be restarted to pick up the policy.
Streamer profile excluded: Game Bar capture is a background app and is intentionally not targeted.
documentationSource: Catalogue mechanism owner: NX01-008 (global enum) - XREF

tweaks.name: Edge background mode disable
tweaks.description: Disables Microsoft Edge background mode through its documented policy (per-user by default).
tweaks.objective: Stop Edge from continuing to run background processes after the last window closes, for owners who prefer that behavior.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxEdgeBackgroundMode (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1): writes BackgroundModeEnabled=0 (DWORD) under HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge (per-user default) or the HKLM policy path with -Scope Machine. This is a documented Edge policy; Microsoft documents that disabling it stops Edge processes from running after the last browser window closes (and related background behavior). The value is journaled before change through the NX11 registry helper and verified by read-back; an already-zero value journals an idempotent skip. No Edge profile, extension or browsing data is touched. Edge must be restarted to read the policy.
tweaks.defaultState: Policy absent: Edge background mode follows the user's edge://settings/system choice.
tweaks.proposedState: BackgroundModeEnabled=0 at the chosen policy scope.

verify.procedure: Read-back of BackgroundModeEnabled equals 0 at the chosen scope; verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the exact prior value (or removes it when it never existed).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue of BackgroundModeEnabled (keyExisted, existed, kind, value) journaled before change.

sideEffects: While Edge is closed, background extensions and background web apps stop running.
No browsing data, profile or extension configuration is changed.
Edge must be restarted before the policy takes effect.

tweaks.name: Edge startup boost disable
tweaks.description: Disables Microsoft Edge startup boost through its documented policy (per-user by default).
tweaks.objective: Stop Edge from preloading at sign-in and restarting in the background, accepting a slower first launch.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxEdgeStartupBoost (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1): writes StartupBoostEnabled=0 (DWORD) under HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge (per-user default) or HKLM with -Scope Machine. Microsoft documents that disabling this policy turns startup boost off, so Edge processes no longer start at OS sign-in and no longer restart in the background after the last window closes. The exact prior value is journaled and verified by read-back; an already-zero value journals a skip. This is a trade-off tweak: the first Edge launch after sign-in may take longer. No profile or browsing data is touched.
tweaks.defaultState: Policy absent: startup boost may be on or off and the user controls it in edge://settings/system.
tweaks.proposedState: StartupBoostEnabled=0 at the chosen policy scope.

verify.procedure: Read-back of StartupBoostEnabled equals 0 at the chosen scope; verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the exact prior value (or removes it when it never existed).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue of StartupBoostEnabled journaled before change.

sideEffects: Edge no longer preloads at sign-in; the first launch can be slower (trade-off stated).
No profile, extension or browsing data is changed.
Edge must be restarted before the policy takes effect.

tweaks.name: Scheduled task inventory report
tweaks.description: Read-only export of every scheduled task with path, state, author, actions and optional per-task XML.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner and NX11-006 a complete, honest task baseline before any selective task decision.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxScheduledTaskInventory (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1) using Get-ScheduledTask; each row carries TaskPath, TaskName, State, Author, Description, action command lines, allow-list membership and protected-pattern status. -IncludeInfo adds last/next run data; -ExportXml writes each task's Export-ScheduledTask XML into an additive backup folder (first backup never overwritten). Nothing is enabled, disabled or modified; the function is strictly read-only. When the ScheduledTasks module is unavailable the result says CmdletUnavailable instead of pretending success. This inventory is the read-only companion to NX11-006 and the source of the mandatory per-task XML backup.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX task inventory exists; tasks remain at their current state.
tweaks.proposedState: Machine-readable task inventory (and optional XML set) available on demand.

verify.procedure: Report returns cmdletAvailable=true and a task array with states; XML files exist for every exported task and match the task path/name.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only inventory; XML export is additive.

originalState.method: Not applicable - read-only; each task's XML is the original-state artifact when exported.

sideEffects: None on task state (read-only).
XML export writes files to the chosen folder and can take time on systems with many tasks.

tweaks.name: Selective scheduled task management
tweaks.description: Enables or disables one allow-listed non-critical task at a time with a per-task XML backup and a verified 3-fallback change.
tweaks.objective: Remove a known, non-critical maintenance/telemetry task only when the owner selects it - never as part of a blanket task sweep.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxScheduledTaskCandidates and Set-NxScheduledTaskState (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). Only the internal allow-list (Application Experience appraiser/updater/startup/PCA/backup, CEIP Consolidator/UsbCeip, SIUF feedback clients, WER QueueReporting, DiskDiagnostic collector, Maps toast/update, WinSAT, Autochk Proxy) may be disabled; anything else is refused. Protected patterns are hard skips: WDI ResolutionHost, UpdateOrchestrator/WindowsUpdate/InstallService, Defender, BitLocker, SystemRestore/WindowsBackup, Registry\RegIdleBackup and TaskScheduler internals. Before any change the task XML is exported (Export-NxTaskState from NX16-006 when loaded, else Export-ScheduledTask directly); if the export fails, the change is refused. The prior State is journaled. The change uses the r1-verified three fallbacks - Disable-ScheduledTask/Enable-ScheduledTask, schtasks /Change, Task Scheduler COM RegisteredTask.Enabled - each re-read via Get-ScheduledTask, up to three rounds; the mechanism used is reported. Failure triggers a best-effort return to the exact prior state and a journaled failure. Rollback is delegated to Invoke-Nx11Rollback and is only-if-ours. Coordination with NX13-013: NX13 owns the telemetry-task curation and reuses Set-Nx11TaskEnabled; eight task names overlap, both entries are idempotent against each other (whichever runs second journals AlreadyApplied), and the coordinator should not select both entries for the same task in one preset.
tweaks.defaultState: All tasks at Windows default state; no NEXTRIX task changes.
tweaks.proposedState: Individually selected allow-listed tasks disabled (or re-enabled), with XML and exact prior state recorded.

verify.procedure: Set-NxScheduledTaskState re-reads the task state after each fallback; success requires the intended Disabled (or non-Disabled on enable) state, journaled with the mechanism and attempts.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores the exact prior State via the same verified 3-fallback engine; a task deleted outside NEXTRIX is reported diverged, never silently recreated.

originalState.method: Per-task Export-ScheduledTask XML plus current State, journaled before the change; XML is mandatory or the change is refused.

sideEffects: The disabled task stops performing its maintenance/telemetry function for all users.
Update, Defender, recovery, WDI and Task Scheduler internal tasks are never offered or touched.
The XML backup is stored under the NEXTRIX backup folder for exact restoration.
documentationSource: research/sources/r1-fsosx-xos.md (DisableScheduledTasks.ps1: 3 fallbacks, per-task verification, protected skip list, counters)

tweaks.name: Resource-heavy process identification report
tweaks.description: Read-only snapshot of the processes using the most working set and cumulative CPU time.
tweaks.objective: Provide evidence for an owner decision without making any claim about performance improvement.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxResourceHeavyProcessReport (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). Enumerates Get-Process and returns two top-N views: working set and cumulative CPU time (seconds since process start). -SampleSeconds adds an interval observation and reports a sampled CPU percentage for processes present in both samples; it does not alter any process. Rows include PID, name, working-set MB, cumulative CPU seconds, sampled percent (when requested), start time, company and path. This is a report only: NEXTRIX never terminates, suspends, throttles or reprioritizes a process here, and the output states that cumulative CPU time is not an instantaneous performance metric.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only top-process report available on demand.

verify.procedure: Report contains topByWorkingSet and topByCpuTime arrays; processCount matches the enumerated process count.

sideEffects: None on processes; -SampleSeconds briefly waits to collect an interval sample.

tweaks.name: Windows Search service configuration
tweaks.description: Configures the WSearch startup type with indexing-scope boundary notes and an SSD/HDD-aware gate.
tweaks.objective: Own the Search SERVICE configuration while indexing scope remains NX01-009's mechanism.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxSearchServiceConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1), which delegates to the shared NX11 service engine. The service record (status plus the authoritative CurrentControlSet Start DWORD) and the dependency report (NX11-019) are captured before any change. Disabling on an SSD or HDD requires explicit acknowledgement (-AcknowledgeMedia) because the trade-off differs by media and because indexing scope is a separate decision; Manual is the declared apply default. Supported startup types are Automatic, Manual and Disabled; -StopService additionally stops a running service (the default changes startup type only, leaving the running instance in place). The exact prior startup type and status are journaled; verification re-reads the Start value; failure restores the exact prior state. Indexing SCOPE (what is indexed) is owned by NX01-009 and is never written here. SSD/HDD guidance is NX06 territory (XREF); the media-scoped disable guidance is reference practice (r5), not a Microsoft performance claim - the documented E1 mechanism is the service startup-type configuration itself.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default WSearch startup type (usually Automatic); no NEXTRIX service change.
tweaks.proposedState: WSearch startup type set to the owner-selected value (Manual by default), journaled and verified.

verify.procedure: Start read-back equals the requested startup type; when -StopService is used the status must also be Stopped. Verify journaled with the dependency verdict.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores the exact journaled startup type and, when the service was originally running, starts it again (only-if-ours).

originalState.method: CurrentControlSet Start DWORD plus live status are journaled before Set-Service.

sideEffects: Manual keeps search/indexing available on demand without automatic startup.
Disabled stops automatic indexing; existing index data remains but search falls back to non-indexed behavior and results may be less complete.
Indexing scope is unchanged - use NX01-009 for scope decisions.
documentationSource: Catalogue XREF: NX01-009 (indexing scope), NX06 (storage guidance)

tweaks.name: SysMain service configuration
tweaks.description: Configures SysMain with RAM and boot-media detection gates and honest research-based warnings.
tweaks.objective: Allow a journaled SysMain startup-type choice only on configurations where the documented trade-off is acceptable.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxSysMainConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1) through the shared NX11 service engine. Detection runs first: total RAM (Win32_ComputerSystem) and the system-disk media type (Get-Partition/Get-Disk/Get-PhysicalDisk, with an honest Unknown fallback). Disabling SysMain is refused on systems below 16 GB RAM unless -AcknowledgeLowMemory is given, and on an HDD boot volume unless -AcknowledgeHdd is given - both gates reflect the r4 UltraOS research that unconditional SysMain disabling can increase hard faults on 8-16 GB systems. Automatic is the restore path. The dependency report (NX11-019) gates running dependents; the exact prior startup type and status are journaled and verified, and failure restores the exact prior state. No performance claim is made; the detected values and the gates are reported with the result. Cross-category note: NX05's memory-compression toggles require SysMain to be running (documented MMAgent error 1058), so a SysMain disable should not be paired with those entries in the same session.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default SysMain startup type; no NEXTRIX service change.
tweaks.proposedState: SysMain startup type set to Disabled only when the RAM/media gates pass or are explicitly acknowledged; otherwise the function skips and reports why.

verify.procedure: Start read-back equals the requested startup type; detection values (RAM GB, media type) and gate outcomes are included in the report; verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores the exact journaled startup type and prior running state (only-if-ours).

originalState.method: CurrentControlSet Start DWORD plus live status, journaled before Set-Service.

sideEffects: On <16 GB systems, disabling SysMain can increase hard faults (research-recorded trade-off, r4).
On HDD boot volumes, prefetch/superfetch behavior is more valuable; the gate protects that case.
NX05 memory-compression changes require SysMain to be running - do not pair them with a SysMain disable.
No memory, pagefile or storage configuration is changed.
documentationSource: research/sources/r4-synergy-ultraos.md (16 GB/NVMe SysMain threshold guidance; blanket-disable rejection)
Catalogue XREF: NX06 storage ownership, NX03 memory boundaries

tweaks.name: Xbox services configuration
tweaks.description: Configures XboxGipSvc and XboxNetApiSvc only, after a dependency report and Game Pass/accessory detection.
tweaks.objective: Offer Xbox service startup control to owners who do not use Xbox/Game Pass, without ever touching Game Pass dependency services.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxXboxServicesConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). Only XboxGipSvc (game-input protocol) and XboxNetApiSvc (Xbox Live networking) are configurable. GamingServices and GamingServicesNet are report-only in the dependency evidence and are always refused as targets because Game Pass install/update/play depends on them (r2 dependency ledger; r5). Detection runs first: Gaming Services packages/registry marker and Xbox input devices; Disabled requires -AcknowledgeGamePass when Game Pass evidence exists and -AcknowledgePeripherals when Xbox devices are present. The NX11-019 dependency report runs for each service; the shared service engine journals exact startup type/status per service and verifies by read-back. Manual is the declared default (stops automatic startup while keeping on-demand activation). Xbox Game Bar's per-user BcastDVRUserService_* capture family is not touched. CONFLICT NX12-005: Xbox app removal and Xbox service management must be resolved together; Game Pass users are excluded.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default Xbox service startup types; Gaming Services untouched.
tweaks.proposedState: XboxGipSvc and XboxNetApiSvc set to the selected startup type (Manual by default), each journaled and verified.

verify.procedure: Per-service start read-back equals the requested type; dependency verdicts and detection evidence are reported; every service verify entry is journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores each service's exact journaled startup type and prior running state (only-if-ours); partial batch results are restorable per service.

originalState.method: Per-service Start DWORD plus status journaled before any change; dependency reports captured in the result.

sideEffects: Xbox accessory management and Xbox Live networking features that use these services degrade when disabled.
Game Pass installs/updates/launches depend on GamingServices/GamingServicesNet - those services are never changed.
Game Bar capture is not affected by this entry.
documentationSource: research/sources/r5-winutil-sophia.md (individual, documented service functions - no blanket list)
Catalogue XREF: NX02-008 dependency report, NX12-005 Xbox app removal conflict
research/sources/r4-synergy-ultraos.md (hardcoded per-user service suffix rejection; BcastDVRUserService_* wildcard)

tweaks.name: Print Spooler configuration
tweaks.description: Read-only Print Spooler report and guidance. NEXTRIX never stops or disables the spooler.
tweaks.objective: Document the spooler's state and the correct owner guidance without creating a disable path that the never-touch policy forbids.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxPrintSpoolerReport (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1) as a REPORT-ONLY entry (status Defined by boundary). Print Spooler ('Spooler') is on registry/schema.json's neverTouchServices list, and tools/Test-NxRegistry.ps1 hard-errors any declarative service action targeting it; the code-side NX11 never-touch guard would also refuse a service change. The function therefore reads the service record (status plus CurrentControlSet Start), enumerates printers via Get-Printer and printer drivers via Get-PrinterDriver when the PrintManagement module is present, and returns explicit guidance: NEXTRIX never stops, disables or reconfigures the spooler even when no printers are detected; removing printing entirely is an owner Windows optional-feature decision outside NEXTRIX automation. No mutation path exists in code, and none may be added without changing the shared schema - a coordinator decision.
tweaks.defaultState: Print Spooler at its Windows default state; no NEXTRIX change.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only report and guidance; no state change is possible from this entry.

verify.procedure: Report returns readOnly=true, neverTouch=true and mutationAvailable=false, with the spooler service record and detected printers/drivers.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no mutation path exists by design.

sideEffects: None (read-only).

tweaks.name: Bluetooth service configuration
tweaks.description: Configures bthserv and BthAvctpSvc only when Bluetooth hardware detection permits it.
tweaks.objective: Offer a journaled Bluetooth service choice for systems with no Bluetooth peripherals, without breaking detected hardware.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxBluetoothServiceConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). Detection enumerates Bluetooth-class PnP devices (Get-PnpDevice, with a Win32_PnPEntity fallback); if any device is present, Disabled is refused unless -AcknowledgePeripherals. The services are configured in dependency order: BthAvctpSvc (the AVCTP dependent) first when disabling, bthserv first when enabling. Each change runs through the shared NX11 service engine: NX11-019 dependency report, exact Start DWORD/status journal, Set-Service, read-back verification, safe-stop restore on failure. XREF NX08-006: Bluetooth peripheral inspection and power policy are owned by NX08; this entry only configures service startup type. No Bluetooth device, driver or pairing is deleted.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default Bluetooth service startup types; hardware untouched.
tweaks.proposedState: bthserv/BthAvctpSvc set to the selected startup type when no Bluetooth hardware gate blocks it; otherwise skipped.

verify.procedure: Per-service Start read-back equals the requested type; detection evidence and gates are reported; verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores each service's exact journaled startup type and prior running state; enabling order is radio service first.

originalState.method: Per-service Start DWORD and status journaled before change.

sideEffects: Bluetooth peripherals stop working when the services are disabled; the detection gate prevents this on systems with hardware unless explicitly acknowledged.
No device, driver or pairing data is removed.
NX08-006 owns Bluetooth power policy.
documentationSource: Catalogue XREF: NX08-006 (Bluetooth peripheral inspection & power policy)

tweaks.name: Fax service configuration
tweaks.description: Configures the legacy Fax service, gated on fax-capable hardware or printers.
tweaks.objective: Allow the legacy Fax service to be disabled only when no fax-capable hardware is detected.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxFaxServiceConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). Detection enumerates PnP entities with 'Fax' in the name and printers whose name or driver mentions Fax; when evidence exists, Disabled is refused unless -AcknowledgeFaxHardware. The shared NX11 service engine captures the exact Start DWORD/status, runs the NX11-019 dependency report, applies Set-Service, verifies by read-back and restores the exact prior state on failure. Disabling the service does not remove the Fax optional component, any document or any print queue. Manual remains available for on-demand use.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default Fax service startup type; hardware untouched.
tweaks.proposedState: Fax startup type set to the selected value when the detection gate permits it.

verify.procedure: Start read-back equals the requested startup type; detection evidence and dependency verdict are reported; verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores the exact journaled startup type and prior running state (only-if-ours).

originalState.method: CurrentControlSet Start DWORD plus status journaled before change.

sideEffects: Fax send/receive through this service stops while disabled.
The Fax optional component and all documents remain installed.

tweaks.name: Remote Registry configuration
tweaks.description: Sets the Remote Registry service to its security-positive default-off state, journaled.
tweaks.objective: Close a remote registry surface on general-purpose systems and keep the change exactly reversible.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxRemoteRegistryConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). Default mode sets RemoteRegistry to Disabled, which Microsoft's security guidance recommends for general-purpose systems. Re-enabling to Manual is allowed only with -AcknowledgeSecurityRisk because it re-exposes a remote surface. The shared NX11 service engine runs the dependency report, captures the exact Start DWORD/status, applies Set-Service, verifies the read-back and restores the exact prior state on failure; every step is journaled. Some enterprise management tools use remote registry access - the trade-off is stated, and rollback can restore the prior startup type and running state.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default RemoteRegistry startup type (often Manual or Disabled depending on edition/policy).
tweaks.proposedState: RemoteRegistry startup type Disabled (security-positive), journaled and verified.

verify.procedure: Start read-back equals Disabled; dependency verdict is reported; verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores the exact journaled startup type and prior running state (only-if-ours).

originalState.method: CurrentControlSet Start DWORD plus status journaled before change.

sideEffects: Remote registry tools and some enterprise management workflows that rely on this service fail while it is disabled.
No local registry access or permissions are changed.

tweaks.name: Windows Error Reporting configuration
tweaks.description: Disables Windows Error Reporting through its documented machine policy, not by disabling WerSvc.
tweaks.objective: Reduce error-reporting activity with the documented, reversible policy while leaving the WER service intact.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxWerReportingConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1): writes the documented machine policy Disabled=1 (DWORD) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting, and Disabled=0 on the Enable path. The policy is verified in the local ErrorReporting.admx (policy WerDisable_2, Machine class, value name Disabled), consistent with the r2 Atlas decision to prefer the documented ErrorReporting policy over a service startup change. WerSvc is NOT stopped or disabled - the service continues to exist and can be restored without a service change. The exact prior policy value is journaled and verified by read-back; an already-set value journals a skip. Diagnostics trade-off is stated: crash reports and WER queue data stop being useful for troubleshooting while disabled. E0 per the catalogue desk assignment: the ADMX policy is authoritative on this machine but no verified Microsoft URL documents this exact policy value, so no E1 upgrade is claimed.
tweaks.defaultState: Policy absent: Windows Error Reporting behavior follows Windows defaults.
tweaks.proposedState: Disabled=1 at the WER machine policy key; WerSvc untouched.

verify.procedure: Read-back of the policy Disabled value equals 1 (or 0 on the Enable path); verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the exact prior policy value, or removes it when it never existed (core registry engine).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue of the WER policy Disabled value journaled before change.

sideEffects: Crash reports and WER queue data stop being collected/sent while disabled - troubleshooting evidence is reduced.
WerSvc remains installed and untouched; the policy is the only changed target.
Some enterprise support workflows that read WER reports are affected.
documentationSource: Local ErrorReporting.admx inspection, build 26300 (2026-11-23): policy WerDisable_2, value 'Disabled'
research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (ErrorReporting policy preferred over WerSvc startup change)

tweaks.name: Maps-related services configuration
tweaks.description: Configures MapsBroker, gated on offline-map usage evidence.
tweaks.objective: Allow the Downloaded Maps Manager startup type to be chosen without breaking installed offline maps.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxMapsServiceConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). Detection checks for the Microsoft.WindowsMaps package and offline map data folders (LocalState\OfflineMaps / MapData) under the current user's package store; when evidence exists, Disabled is refused unless -AcknowledgeOfflineMaps. Manual is the declared default, keeping on-demand map use possible. The shared NX11 service engine captures the exact Start DWORD/status, runs the NX11-019 dependency report, applies Set-Service, verifies by read-back and restores the exact prior state on failure. No map data, app package or download is deleted.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default MapsBroker startup type; map data untouched.
tweaks.proposedState: MapsBroker startup type set to the selected value when the offline-map gate permits it.

verify.procedure: Start read-back equals the requested startup type; offline-map evidence and gate outcome are reported; verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores the exact journaled startup type and prior running state (only-if-ours).

originalState.method: CurrentControlSet Start DWORD plus status journaled before change.

sideEffects: With MapsBroker disabled, offline map updates and map-related background operations stop; Manual keeps on-demand use.
Installed map data and the Maps app are never deleted.

tweaks.name: DiagTrack (Connected User Experiences) configuration
tweaks.description: Configures the DiagTrack service startup type, coordinated with the NX13 telemetry policy set.
tweaks.objective: Provide a journaled service-level DiagTrack choice while NX13 remains the owner of telemetry policy.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxDiagTrackConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1) through the shared NX11 service engine: NX11-019 dependency report, exact Start DWORD/status journal, Set-Service, read-back verification, safe-stop restore. NX13 owns the telemetry policy set (AllowTelemetry and related values); this entry configures only the Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service and makes no privacy claim. NEXTRIX does not block DiagTrack firewall rule groups (the r5 WinUtil pattern is deliberately not reproduced). Documented impact is surfaced: Xbox achievements and Feedback Hub can be affected (r5). The service is conditional; it is never part of a blanket service list.

tweaks.proposedState: DiagTrack startup type set to the selected value, journaled and verified; telemetry policy remains NX13's decision.

verify.procedure: Start read-back equals the requested startup type; dependency verdict is reported; verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores the exact journaled startup type and prior running state (only-if-ours).

tweaks.name: Third-party service inventory & selective configuration
tweaks.description: Read-only inventory of non-Microsoft services plus one-service-at-a-time configuration with explicit consent.
tweaks.objective: Let the owner see and selectively configure vendor services without a blanket list or Windows-component risk.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxThirdPartyServiceInventory and Set-NxThirdPartyServiceConfig (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). The inventory enumerates Win32_Service, excludes services whose binary lives under %SystemRoot% (Windows components), excludes never-touch names, and reports name/display/state/startMode/startName/path/dependencies. Configuration requires the exact service name, -ConfirmService (per-service consent) and the shared NX11 service engine; it refuses never-touch names and refuses Windows-component binaries. Every change runs the NX11-019 dependency report, journals the exact Start DWORD/status, verifies by read-back and restores the exact state on failure. Vendor dependency guidance remains the owner's responsibility - NEXTRIX never claims knowledge of third-party service semantics.
tweaks.defaultState: Vendor services at their installed startup types; no NEXTRIX change.
tweaks.proposedState: One owner-selected non-Microsoft service set to the chosen startup type, journaled and verified.

verify.procedure: Inventory lists non-Microsoft services only; Set-NxThirdPartyServiceConfig re-reads the Start value and must match the requested startup type; verify journaled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx11Rollback restores the exact journaled startup type and prior running state (only-if-ours).

originalState.method: CurrentControlSet Start DWORD plus status journaled before change, after the inventory record is captured.

sideEffects: Changing a vendor service can break the vendor application; explicit consent and vendor guidance are required.
Windows-component services and never-touch names are refused.
Exactly one service is changed per call.

tweaks.name: Service dependency inspection engine
tweaks.description: Read-only dependency gate: reports required services, dependents, protected dependents and a safety verdict for any service change.
tweaks.objective: Make every NX11 service change start from an explicit dependency report, never from a service name alone.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxServiceDependencyReport (src/nxcore/functions/NX11.ps1). With -ServiceName it returns the authoritative service record (status, CurrentControlSet Start, delayed-autostart), binary path (Win32_Service), required services, dependent services with running/never-touch flags, and a verdict: ServiceMissing, RefuseProtectedDependents (a never-touch service depends on this one), RequiresDependentAcknowledgement (running dependents), or SafeForStartupChange. Without -ServiceName it returns a machine-wide summary of every service that has dependents. The shared NX11 service engine calls it before every Set-Service; protected dependents are a hard refusal and running dependents require explicit acknowledgement before Disabled. The function is strictly read-only - it never starts, stops or reconfigures anything. Downstream categories may call it as the service-change gate.
tweaks.proposedState: Machine-readable dependency verdict available before every service change.

verify.procedure: Detailed mode returns service, startType, requiredServices, dependentServices, runningDependents, protectedDependents and verdict; summary mode returns servicesWithDependents.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
